title: Largest natural satellites — facets of the Solar System
description: Each entry is a Facet of the Solar System: a natural satellite shown by its size face (mean diameter) and the planet it orbits. Where /2 (Structures) held the planets themselves, /3 (Facets) holds the moons — the faces those planets present through their satellites.

provenance.primary_source: NASA — planetary science pages (science.nasa.gov) and JPL
provenance.note: Public-domain NASA/JPL values, mean diameters in km, rounded for a compact facet table. Ganymede and Titan both exceed the planet Mercury in size (though not mass).

facets.name: Ganymede
facets.note: largest moon in the Solar System
